 8th Pay Commission Latest: 2.57 Fitment Factor, 7% Annual Increment – Salary Hike & Arrears From January 2026?
 Personal Finance oi-Pooja Jaiswar By Pooja Jaiswar 
 Updated: Monday, November 16, 2026, 16:41 [IST]
 Add as a preferred source on Google Once again, new recommendations have made it online for the much-awaited 8th Pay Commission. This time the combination of fitment factor and annual increment is being debated and scrutinized. A level 1 grade employee has the potential to earn up to Rs 60,637 per month by his or her fifth year in the government office if the fitment factor is 2.57 and the annual increment is 7%.
 Although 8th CPC recommendations are expected to be implemented in the fiscal year 2027-28, the effective date is highly desired to be January 1, 2026, since 7th Pay Commission ended on December 31, 2025. If the effective date is fixed for January 2026, then employees and pensioners will receive a significant salary increase and arrears.
 The recommendations for the 8th Pay Commission are yet to be finalized, and a final report is likely to be submitted in May 2027. Till then, several employee unions and pensioners' bodies have submitted their demands that could boost the cost of life for the employees and retirees.
 8th Pay Commission Fitment Factor + Annual Increment
 Several employee unions and bodies have recommended their desired fitment factor. The Bharatiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh (BPMS) has suggested the extraordinary 4 fitment factor, while the National Council - Joint Consultative Machinery (NC-JCM), Staff Side, All India Defence Employees' Federation (AIDEF), Bharat Pensioners Samaj (BPS), and All India New Pension Scheme Employees Federation (AINPSEF) have recommended a fitment factor of 3.8333. The Maharashtra Old Pension Organisation has suggested 3.80.
 Now some of these unions have also recommended an annual increment alongside the fitment factor. The NC-JCM, AIDEF, and the Federation of National Postal Organisations (FNPO) have recommended an annual increment to be increased to 6%. While the AINPSEF has proposed an annual increment of 7%.

 Currently, central government employees receive a 3% annual increment under 7th Pay Commission, while the fitment factor stands at 2.57. The basic salary is Rs 18,000 per month for level 1 grader, while level 2, level 3, and level 4 grade employees earn up to Rs 19,900, Rs 21,700, and Rs 25,500 per month. A level 5 grade employee gets Rs 29,200 per month currently.
 What is the difference between fitment factor and annual increment?
 In simple words, the fitment factor is the one-time benchmark implemented to revise basic pay from the previous pay commission to the current. So, a fitment factor will only be a one-time hike in basic salary as the government employees shift from 7th Pay Commission to 8th Pay Commission.
 On the other hand, an annual increment is a recurring increase in existing pay on an annual basis. This means a 3% annual increment was carried every year throughout the 7th Pay Commission timeline.
 Let's take an illustration to understand which fitment factor and annual increment would boost employees' basic salary to the maximum under 8th Pay Commission:
 Scenario 1: 2.57 fitment factor + 3% annual increment
 If the fitment factor is hiked to 2.57 under the 8th CPC, the level 1 basic salary would rise to Rs 46,260 per month. This will be a one-time hike in the first year. Then a 3% 3% annual increment is applied for four years after the initial revision. This will translate to 1.03 means 103% of the previous year's basic pay. The (1.03)⁴ represents a 3% annual increment compounded over four years.
 Rs 46,260 x (1.03)⁴ = Rs 52,066 in the fifth year.
 Rs 46,260 x (1.03)⁹ = Rs 60,359 in the tenth year.
 Applying the similar formula, the level grade 2 basic pay will rise to Rs 51,143 in the first year at 2.57 fitment from Rs 19,900 basic pay. The 3% increment would lead to salary increase to Rs 57,562 per month in the fifth year and Rs 66,730 per month in the 10th year.
 Scenario 2: 2.1 fitment factor + 7% annual increment
 However, in the second scenario, the fitment factor was lowered to 2.1 and the annual increment increased to 7%. Then level 1 grade employee's basic pay would increase to Rs 37,800 at fitment of 2.1 and his or her 7% annual increment would lead to Rs 49,548 basic pay in fifth year and to Rs 69,494 in tenth year.
 Scenario 3: 2.57 fitment factor + 7% annual increment
 Presumably if the fitment factor is fixed at 2.57 and the annual increment at 7% then level 1 grade employees' basic pay would rise to Rs 46,260, which is unchanged from the first scenario. A similar revision will be seen across level 2-5 grade employees as well.
 However, a 7% increment could increase salary in the coming years significantly. For level 1 grade employees, their basic pay could reach to Rs 60,637 in the fifth year and to Rs 85,047 per month in the tenth year of service due to 7% annual increment.
 These are just illustrations and not the official recommendations by the government for 8th CPC.

 8th Pay Commission Arrears Hike
 The final report of 8th CPC is expected to be submitted on May 5, 2027, and the implementation date will be followed thereafter once the government makes the final approval.
 Historically, arrears were paid in two installments under the 5th Pay Commission between 1997-98 and 1998-99. While in the 6th Pay Commission, arrears paid paid, with additional fiscal expenditure estimated to be around 0.77% of the GDP in 2009-10. In the 7th Pay Commission, the recommendations were implemented on time from January 1, 2016, at the end of the cycle of the 6th Pay Commission, which avoided the arrears burden.
 However, since the 8th CPC is expected to be implemented in 2027 or early 2028, central government employees are starting to pay 12-month pending arrears of 2026 if the effective date is settled at January 1, 2026.
 Particulars 5th Pay Commission 6th Pay Commission 7th Pay Commission 
 Period of implementation / reference 1997-98 and 1998-99 2009-10 Effective from January 1, 2016 
 Arrears payment approach Arrears were paid in two instalments. Arrears were paid following implementation of recommendations. Recommendations took effect from January 1, 2016, at the end of the 10-year cycle. 
 Number of instalments Two instalments Not specified in the given source No significant arrears burden was highlighted. 
 Payment timeline Spread across two financial years: 1997-98 and 1998-99. Additional expenditure was recorded in 2009-10. Effective date was January 1, 2016. 
 Financial impact Payments were distributed over two financial years. Additional expenditure estimated at 0.77% of GDP in 2009-10. Largely avoided a significant arrears burden. 
 Impact on government expenditure Financial burden was spread over two years. Arrears created a noticeable fiscal expenditure burden. No significant arrears burden was highlighted in the comparison. 
 Key government approach Phased payment of arrears. Payment of arrears with additional fiscal expenditure. Timely implementation at the end of the 10-year cycle. 
 Major takeaway Arrears were not paid entirely in one financial year. The financial implications of arrears became a concern but were managed. Implementation largely avoided a substantial accumulated arrears burden.
